sources.role: Official Windows XEBRA distribution; executable, simulation image and documentation
Official XEBRA for PC instructions covering OSROM, controller setup, per-game INI files and image formats

paths.path: XEBRA.ini beside the CD-ROM image for per-game initial settings; XEBRA's working directory for shared runtime assets
paths.naming: For an image named <game>.img, the official PC instructions specify <game>.ini; the bundled XEBRA.TXT documents XEBRA.AR and simulation images

paths.path: View / Controller... interactive dialog in XEBRA.EXE; PC pad buttons and X/Y/Z/R/U/V axes are sampled at startup/dialog time
paths.naming: Associations are selected interactively by PS1 port, controller type, PC button and axis; no verified portable mapping-file grammar

paths.path: XEBRA's Memory Card 1 and Memory Card 2 images selected through File / Memory Card...
paths.naming: The documented memory-card images are commonly named BU00 and BU10

paths.path: XEBRA.RUN, <product-id>.RI0, and <product-id>.RI1 in the XEBRA working directory
paths.naming: F1/F7 use XEBRA.RUN; F2/F8 use <product-id>.RI0; F3/F9 use <product-id>.RI1

paths.path: OSROM (no extension) beside XEBRA.EXE, or the compatible OS ROM bundled by XEBRA
paths.naming: The official PC instructions require an official PS1 OS ROM to be renamed OSROM with no extension
No external cryptographic or decryption-key file is consumed by the documented XEBRA PC contract

windows.notes: The official PC page documents a Windows XEBRA.EXE workflow. XEBRA also has an Android identity on the official page, but Android is outside this four-host catalog.

linux.reason: The official distribution is a Windows XEBRA.EXE archive and no native Linux build or source-backed Linux persistence contract is published.

linux-flatpak.reason: No XEBRA Flatpak package or manifest is published by the official distribution page.

macos.reason: The official PC distribution is Windows-only and publishes no native macOS build or source-backed macOS persistence contract.

controller_boundary.refusal: Do not invent a XEBRA controller writer: the official PC instructions require runtime host-pad/button and axis probing plus interactive association, while no verified persistent mapping grammar or device identity contract is available.

notes: The official XEBRA archive was downloaded and SHA-256 verified. State and memory-card filenames are documented, but Windows launch and effective controller input were not runtime verified.
